acro-suites-crete.title: Acro Suites Guide — Agia Pelagia, Crete | Suites With Keith
acro-suites-crete.description: Keith's guide to Acro Suites on Crete — an adults-only cliffside wellbeing resort above Mononaftis Bay, where all 49 suites and villas have private pools.
acro-suites-crete.tagline: An adults-only wellbeing resort built into the cliff above Mononaftis Bay — Santorini drama at Crete value.

stats.label: Suites & Villas — Every One With A Private Pool
Per Night In September (Approx. — Ask Me For Exact Dates)

intro_paras: Acro Suites is the reason I put Crete on the matrix. Opened in 2021 on the cliffs above Mononaftis Bay at Agia Pelagia — about half an hour from Heraklion's airport — it's a wellbeing resort in the real sense: adults only, built down the rock face in tiers, with every one of its 49 suites and villas holding its own private pool.

The headline act is the cave suites, carved into the cliff with heated grotto pools — the closest thing to Santorini's cave-hotel drama anywhere outside Santorini, at a fraction of the caldera's prices and none of its crowds.

It's also quietly one of the best-fed resorts on the island: Cremnos for modern Greek with the sea below you, UMI for Nikkei — Japanese-Peruvian, and better than it has any right to be this far from a city — and Eleonas for authentic Cretan cooking amid the olive trees.
See Where Crete Sits On The Island Matrix →

glance.html: Crete — north coast, 30 min from Heraklion airport

glance.label: Perfect For
glance.html: Couples, honeymoons, spa & yoga travelers, design lovers

sections.h3: The Details That Made The List

notes.b: Every unit has a private pool.
notes.t: From the entry-level Wave Suite up to the Acroterra Villa, there is no category where you're sharing your swim.
Dome-roofed, carved into the cliff, with heated grotto pools — the rooms the property is known for, and the ones to book early.
Cremnos (modern Greek), UMI (Nikkei), and Eleonas (Cretan, in the olive groves) — you can stay a week without repeating a dinner.
A Byzantine-inspired hammam, Finnish sauna, heated indoor pool and cold plunge, plus the Asana Yoga Shala for daily practice. The "wellbeing resort" label is earned, not marketing.

sections.h3: The Fine Print

notes.t: This is a no-children property — for a family trip to this coast, I book Minos Beach Art Hotel instead.
The tiered layout means stairs and steep paths — dramatic to look at, less ideal if mobility is a concern.
Agia Pelagia is a base, not a destination — you'll want wheels for Heraklion, the Knossos ruins, and the beaches further west.
The sea is at its warmest, the crowds have thinned, and rates come off their August peak.

sections.take: If you want Santorini's cliff-edge drama without Santorini's prices or crowds, this is the booking.

capella-sydney.title: Capella Sydney — First Look & Rates Guide | Suites With Keith
capella-sydney.description: A researched first look at Capella Sydney — the 1930s sandstone landmark turned Sydney's most polished luxury hotel. Rooms, dining, Auriga Spa, and what rates to expect.
capella-sydney.tagline: A 1930s sandstone landmark reborn as the city's most polished luxury address — steps from Circular Quay, the Opera House, and the Royal Botanic Garden.

stats.label: Average Entry Room — Huge For Sydney
Heated Indoor Pool At Auriga Spa

intro_paras: Unlike my Greece guides, this one isn't from a stay — yet. But when clients ask where to base a Sydney trip, this is the property I keep coming back to, and here's the researched case for it.

Capella Sydney opened in March 2023 inside the former Department of Education building — a heritage sandstone landmark on Farrer Place, completed in 1930 and transformed over seven years into Capella Hotel Group's first Australian property. The location is the CBD's best: a short walk to Circular Quay, the Opera House, the Royal Botanic Garden, and the harbour itself.

What sets it apart on paper is space and restraint. The 192 rooms and suites average more than 50 square metres at entry level — enormous by Sydney standards — rising to four Prestige Suites of up to roughly 235 square metres. Dining is anchored by Brasserie 1930, which has earned two hats (Australia's Michelin-star equivalent), alongside McRae Bar and the garden-atrium Aperture. And the top-floor Auriga Spa — moon-phase-inspired treatments, a Connect to Country ritual developed with Aboriginal elders, a 20-metre heated indoor pool, Technogym fitness, steam and sauna — is widely considered the city's finest hotel wellness floor.

glance.html: Farrer Place, Sydney CBD — walk to Circular Quay & the Opera House

notes.b: The rooms are the biggest in their class.
notes.t: Entry categories averaging 50+ square metres is practically unheard of in Sydney's CBD — most competitors start in the 30s.
The Australian equivalent of Michelin recognition, on property, celebrating Australian produce — with McRae Bar and Aperture rounding out the food and drink.

notes.b: Auriga Spa is the city's benchmark wellness floor.
notes.t: A 20-metre heated indoor pool under the roofline, treatments with Synthesis Organics, and the Connect to Country hot-stone ritual created with Aboriginal elders.

notes.b: The building itself is the amenity.
notes.t: Seven years of restoration turned a 1930 Beaux-Arts government landmark into the rare new-build luxury hotel with a genuine sense of place.

sections.h3: The Fine Print

notes.t: At the time of writing, entry rooms generally land around AUD $800–$1,300 per night (roughly USD $525–$850), with Sydney's peak dates — summer, New Year's Eve, major events — pushing meaningfully higher. Suites start well above that. I'll always quote your exact dates before you commit.

notes.b: It's a city-harbour hotel, not a harbour-view hotel.
notes.t: The building sits a few blocks inland — the trade is heritage grandeur and space over water directly outside the window. For a view-first stay, I'd pair or compare it with a harbour-facing alternative.
Australian summer is December–February. A shoulder-season stay (autumn or spring) buys noticeably better rates and gentler weather for walking the city.

sections.take: On paper — and by every serious review I trust — this is currently the hotel to beat in Sydney. When I've walked it myself, this page will graduate from first look to full review.

cheval-blanc-paris.title: Cheval Blanc Paris Review — Paris, France | Suites With Keith
cheval-blanc-paris.description: Why Cheval Blanc Paris is on Keith's featured Paris list — LVMH's 72-room showpiece above La Samaritaine, with the Dior Spa and Langosteria over the Seine.
cheval-blanc-paris.tagline: LVMH's showpiece above La Samaritaine — just 72 rooms, Dior Spa, and the most coveted new address in Paris.
intro_paras: Every era of Paris gets one new hotel that everyone wants, and this era's is Cheval Blanc. LVMH rebuilt the top of La Samaritaine — the Art Deco department store at Pont-Neuf — into just 72 rooms and suites hanging directly over the Seine.

The scale is the point. Seventy-two keys in a city where the grand palaces run three hundred means the service ratio is absurd, the public spaces never feel public, and a river-view room actually means the river filling your window. The Dior Spa is the brand's flagship, the pool is one of the longest in Paris, and Langosteria on the seventh floor is the Italian table the whole city fights over.

This is the booking for clients who've done the classic palaces and want the modern one — design-forward, fashion-adjacent, and genuinely hard to get in season. As a Fora advisor I book it with palace-level perks, and lead time matters more here than anywhere else in Paris.

notes.t: A fraction of the size of the classic palaces — the service ratio and privacy are unlike anything else at this level in Paris.
The house flagship, with a 30-metre pool — the best spa-and-swim combination in the city.
The Milan seafood institution's Paris outpost, seven floors up with the Seine and Pont-Neuf below.

notes.t: Seventy-two rooms and the whole world asking — for spring, summer or fashion weeks, this is a months-ahead conversation, not a weeks-ahead one.
If your Paris dream is chandeliers and Louis XV, the Ritz or the Crillon is the better match — this is contemporary glamour.
Pont-Neuf puts the Louvre, the Marais and Saint-Germain all within fifteen minutes on foot — the most walkable base of any Paris palace.

claridges-london.title: Claridge's Review — London, England | Suites With Keith
claridges-london.description: Why Claridge's is on Keith's featured London list — the art deco icon and London's definitive grande dame, from the foyer tea to suites like private Mayfair flats.
claridges-london.tagline: The art deco icon and London's definitive grande dame — impeccable service theater, the famous foyer tea, and suites that feel like private Mayfair flats.
intro_paras: Every city has a hotel that defines it, and London's is Claridge's. A fixture of Mayfair since 1856 and the art deco masterpiece of the 1920s rebuild, it has hosted every royal family in Europe and never once seemed impressed with itself for it.

What keeps it at the top isn't nostalgia — it's the service, which runs with a warmth and precision that other hotels study. Afternoon tea in the Foyer under the Chihuly chandelier is the version every other tea is measured against, and the rooms manage the trick of feeling like the private flat of a very stylish friend.
For a first serious London trip, a celebration, or anyone who wants the full English hotel experience executed perfectly, this is where I start the conversation.

connaught-london.description: Why The Connaught is on Keith's featured London list — quieter and clubbier than Claridge's, with the Connaught Bar and the most discreet service in the city.
connaught-london.tagline: Quieter and clubbier than its sibling Claridge's — home to the Connaught Bar, Hélène Darroze's dining room, and the most discreet service in the city.
intro_paras: If Claridge's is London's stage, The Connaught is its private club. Tucked onto Carlos Place in the quietest corner of Mayfair, it trades spectacle for discretion — the hotel where the service anticipates rather than performs.

The Connaught Bar has spent years trading the 'World's Best Bar' title with a handful of rivals, and its tableside martini trolley is a London ritual. Hélène Darroze's dining room holds three Michelin stars, the Aman Spa is one of only two in Europe, and the famous mahogany staircase has been polished by a century of the world's most private guests.
I book it for repeat London visitors, for anyone who values being left alone beautifully, and for couples who'd rather have the best bar in the world downstairs than a scene in the lobby.

ellerman-house-cape-town.tagline: A 13-room Relais & Châteaux house above the Atlantic with a private art collection and wine gallery — the gateway stay before or after safari, and reason enough to linger.
intro_paras: Ellerman House is what happens when a grand Edwardian mansion on Bantry Bay stays in caring hands: thirteen rooms, a cliff-side lawn over the Atlantic, and the feeling of staying in the home of a spectacularly good host.

The house holds one of the finest private collections of South African art anywhere — over a thousand works through the rooms and gardens — and a wine gallery whose cellar runs thousands of bottles deep in Cape benchmarks. Breakfast is cooked to order, the pantry is open all day, and almost everything is included in the rate.
I use it as the Cape Town bookend for safari itineraries — a few days here before the bush resets the jet lag in style — but clients routinely tell me it was the stay they'd repeat first.

four-seasons-tamarindo.description: Why Four Seasons Tamarindo made Keith's Mexico shortlist — a 3,000-acre private reserve on the Costalegre coast with dramatic clifftop pools and barely another soul in sight.
four-seasons-tamarindo.tagline: A 3,000-acre private reserve on the Costalegre coast — dramatic clifftop pools, protected wilderness, and barely another soul in sight.
intro_paras: Tamarindo is what happens when Four Seasons is handed an entire stretch of protected coastline: a resort woven into a 3,000-acre private reserve on the Costalegre — the "happy coast" south of Puerto Vallarta that most travelers have never heard of, which is precisely its appeal.

The architecture alone earns the trip — terraced stone, cascading clifftop pools, and rooms that frame the Pacific like gallery pieces. But the real luxury is the emptiness: private beaches, a golf course through the jungle, and a coastline with nothing else on it.
I recommend it for travelers who've done Cabo and Punta Mita and want Mexico with the volume turned all the way down — and for anyone who books hotels for the design.

londolozi-south-africa.description: Why Londolozi is on Keith's featured safari list — the family-run Sabi Sand reserve that set the standard for leopard viewing worldwide.
londolozi-south-africa.eyebrow: Hotel Guides · Sabi Sand, South Africa
londolozi-south-africa.tagline: The family-run reserve that set the standard for leopard viewing worldwide — five camps, one ethos, and guiding that turns first-timers into safari people for life.
intro_paras: Ask any guide in Africa where to see leopards and one name comes back: Londolozi. The Varty family has run this stretch of the Sabi Sand since 1926, and four generations of habituation work mean the world's most elusive big cat walks past vehicles here like you're not there.

Five camps share the reserve — from the family-friendly Varty Camp to the rarefied Private Granite Suites — all run on the same ethos: conservation first, guiding as a craft, and hospitality that feels like being hosted rather than processed. The storytelling around the fire is as much a part of the experience as the drives.
This is the safari I recommend when someone wants the real thing at the highest level — the place that turns a first safari into a lifelong habit.

luura-paros.title: Luura Guide — Cliff, Paros | Suites With Keith
luura-paros.description: Keith's guide to LUURA on Paros — the Morgans Originals clifftop newcomer above Agia Irini bay, opened August 2026, with 39 adults-only suites facing Antiparos.
luura-paros.tagline: The newest hotel on Paros — a clifftop, adults-only Morgans Originals debut above Agia Irini bay, facing the Antiparos sunset.

stats.label: Opened Weeks Ago — The Inaugural Season

intro_paras: Luura is the hotel my Paros clients ask about most, and as of August 2026 it finally exists: the first Greek property in Ennismore's Morgans Originals collection, opened on the cliffs above Agia Irini bay on the island's west coast, looking straight at Antiparos and the sunset.

It's the project of Vivium — the family office of art patron Elie Khoury, working with his daughter Sophie — and it shows in the collection hanging on the walls: Francesco Clemente, Claire Tabouret, Tschabalala Self, alongside Greek artists. The buildings, by Elastic Architects with Berlin's Lambs and Lions on interiors, cluster like a whitewashed village above the water.

The 39 suites are adults-only, every one with a private terrace or garden and a sea view, nineteen of them with private pools. And the restaurant bet is bold: a cliffside outpost of Mimi Kakushi, the acclaimed Dubai contemporary-Japanese room, next to Lenea's Mediterranean menu — nothing else on Paros is attempting anything like it.
Read My Full Paros Guide →

glance.label: Perfect For
glance.html: Design & art lovers, couples, sunset seekers, early adopters

sections.h3: The Details That Made The List

notes.t: The hotel opened August 1, 2026 — this is the rare chance to know a property before the rest of the world posts it.
Most of the island's luxury clusters around Naoussa in the northeast; Luura faces west over Agia Irini bay toward Antiparos, which means sunset from your terrace, not from a crowded bar.
The Dubai Japanese restaurant's first Greek outpost, plus Lenea for Mediterranean and a pool restaurant — a serious food program for a 39-key hotel.
Sauna and cold-plunge contrast therapy, treatments built on essential-oil blends developed with a Greek herbalist, daily breathwork and movement.

sections.h3: The Fine Print

notes.t: For a family trip to Paros, Cosme and Parīlio are the bookings.
Luura sits on the opposite coast — plan on a car, and treat the hotel as a destination rather than a base for town evenings.
Brand-new hotels iterate through their first summer. I track how openings actually settle — ask me for the current read before you commit a honeymoon to it.

The hotel is too new for reliable published pricing — I'll quote exact dates directly, and current opening offers have included a free night on longer stays plus transfers, breakfast, and hotel credit.

intro_paras: Minos Beach opened in 1963 and was arguably Crete's first true luxury hotel — the vision of hotelier Eleni Nakou at the dawn of Greek tourism's golden era. Sixty years on, it's still run by the founding Mamidakis family's bluegr group, and it has aged the way the best things do: established, shaded, unhurried.

The setup is simple and hasn't needed changing: 125 whitewashed bungalows, villas and suites scattered through waterfront gardens on Mirabello Bay, none more than about twenty steps from the sea. What makes it singular is the art — more than 55 site-specific sculptures and installations curated by the family's foundation turn the grounds into an open-air museum you wander barefoot.
It's also the rare hotel of this calibre that genuinely welcomes children — multi-bedroom villas, babysitting, bikes, watersports — which is exactly why it's my family pick for eastern Crete.

mombo-camp-botswana.tagline: Botswana's most storied camp, on an island in the Delta's richest game country — water and land safari in one, at the top of the category.
intro_paras: In the safari world, Mombo is spoken of the way sommeliers speak of a legendary vintage. Wilderness's flagship sits on Chief's Island in the Moremi Reserve, the heart of the Okavango Delta, surrounded by what is widely considered the richest concentration of game in Botswana.

The camp raises tented luxury to its ceiling — vast suites on raised walkways, plunge pools looking over the floodplain, and a staff that runs one of the smoothest operations in Africa. Because the Delta floods seasonally, the safari here is double-sided: classic game drives and water-based exploring, in one stay.

Botswana's model is low-volume, high-value tourism — fewer vehicles, emptier wilderness, higher rates — and Mombo is that philosophy at its peak. This is the connoisseur's safari, and the one wildlife film crews keep coming back to.

odera-tinos.description: Keith's guide to Odera on Tinos — the island's first five-star hotel, above Vourni beach near Kionia: 77 sea-view rooms and pool suites, three restaurants, and a 280 sqm spa.
odera-tinos.tagline: The first five-star hotel on Tinos — Tinian stone above Vourni beach, on the island where eating and walking are the itinerary.

stats.label: First Luxury Hotel In Tinos History — Opened 2024
Per Night In September (Approx. — Ask Me For Exact Dates)

intro_paras: For decades Tinos was the great Cycladic island with nowhere serious to sleep — extraordinary food, marble villages, dovecotes, pilgrimage crowds, and pensions. Odera, opened in May 2024 above Vourni beach near Kionia, changed that in one stroke: the island's first five-star hotel, now flying Marriott's Autograph Collection flag.

The design earns the setting. Cubic volumes of Tinian slate and stone cluster down the hillside like one of the island's own villages — architecture by Panos Nikolaidis, interiors by Studio Bonarchi, and a shortlisting at the AHEAD Europe awards in its first year. Of the 77 keys, 54 are pool suites; every room faces the Aegean, and the sunsets here are the island's best-kept secret.

What sells it for me is how well it understands its island. Three restaurants — Eos, the Apollo pool bar, and the taverna-style Nosti on the beach — lean hard into Tinian produce and wine, and the hotel sits eight minutes from the port and Chora, at the trailhead of the walking country that makes Tinos worth the trip.

perma-serifos.description: Keith's guide to Perma on Serifos — five stone residences by MOLD Architects above a secluded cove at Lia, each with a private pool and outdoor kitchen. Adults only.
perma-serifos.tagline: Five stone residences above a secluded cove — an adults-only wellbeing sanctuary on the island that never got a scene.

stats.label: Residences — Each With Private Pool & Outdoor Kitchen

intro_paras: Perma opened in 2025 with exactly five keys, and that number is the whole philosophy. Carved into a rocky slope above a secluded cove at Lia — a few minutes from Livadi port and the hill-climbing Chora — it's the work of MOLD Architects, the Athens studio of Iliana Kerestetzi, and the design press (Dezeen, Designboom, ArchDaily) got to it before the travel press did. That tells you what kind of place it is.

The name comes from the PERMA model of positive psychology, and the property is built as an adults-only wellbeing sanctuary: a yoga shala, sound baths, a serious massage menu, and no schedule telling you when to do any of it. Stone excavated during construction became the walls; the roofs are planted; rainwater is collected. It disappears into the hillside on purpose.

Every residence has a private pool and — the detail I love — a fully equipped outdoor kitchen. There's no restaurant and no bar: breakfast comes from local ingredients, and evenings are yours to cook under your own pergola with the sea below. On Serifos, that isn't a compromise. It's the point.

MOLD Architects built it from the site's own excavated stone with planted roofs and sliding glass walls — it's been published by Dezeen, Designboom, and ArchDaily within a year of opening.
Each residence's terrace is set up to actually cook — pair it with the port fishmongers in Livadi and you have the best dinner reservation on Serifos.
Yoga shala, sound healing, massages in your residence — offered, never imposed.

notes.b: No restaurant, no bar, adults only.
notes.t: If you want to be waited on nightly, this is the wrong booking — and knowing that is exactly how to book it right.
Five units on an under-visited island: the summer calendar effectively sells out to people who planned the year before.

notes.b: Rent a car and use it.
notes.t: Serifos rewards driving — empty beaches, the Chora climb, tavernas in Livadi ten minutes away. Lia Beach itself is a short walk below.

notes.t: September is the month I'd choose: warm sea, low light, nobody around.

intro_paras: Some hotels have a location; this one has a chapter of history. The result is unlike anything else in the city: two miles of corridors, a grand marble staircase built for generals, guestrooms in former ministers' offices, and nine restaurants and bars including Mauro Colagreco's three-Michelin-pedigree flagship. intro_paras: There are grand hotels, and then there is the hotel the word comes from. César Ritz opened his masterpiece on Place Vendôme in 1898, Escoffier ran the kitchen, and a century of legends followed — Coco Chanel lived here for decades, Hemingway 'liberated' the bar that now carries his name.

The four-year restoration brought it all back to full shine: the gilded salons, the garden, the Ritz Club pool downstairs that looks like a Roman bath, and Bar Hemingway pouring what many consider the best martini in Europe. It is unapologetically classic — this is the gilt-and-brocade Paris fantasy, executed at the highest level in the world.
I send clients here for the once-in-a-lifetime trips: milestone anniversaries, the honeymoon that has to be perfect, the mother-daughter trip she'll never stop talking about. Nobody regrets the Ritz.

glance.html: Families and couples both, loyalists, low-key beach weeks

sections.h3: The Details That Made The List

notes.t: The St. Regis signature translated to the beach — unpacked, pressed, and the day arranged before breakfast.
Casitas in gardens rather than towers on a strip — the quietest luxury on this stretch of the Pacific.
Gated, green and genuinely beautiful — with golf, surf and Sayulita's color a short drive away.

sections.h3: The Fine Print, From Your Advisor

notes.t: Families are welcome and well served; couples who want a fully adult resort should look at Naviva next door.
Beautiful, swimmable in the coves, but this is ocean, not Caribbean bathwater — the pools carry the calm-water duty.
For Marriott loyalists this is a marquee redemption — tell me your dates and I'll layer my Fora perks on top.

sections.take: The quiet, polished way to do Punta Mita — residential calm, real butler service, and the peninsula's best of both worlds.

st-regis-punta-mita.perks_eyebrow: Book the St. Regis Through Me
st-regis-punta-mita.perks_p: Rates through me are identical to booking direct — the perks are not. As a Fora advisor, my clients receive a space-available upgrade, daily breakfast, and a hotel credit — plus my direct line to the team on property before and during your stay.
st-regis-punta-mita.cta_eyebrow: Planning A Trip To Punta Mita?
st-regis-punta-mita.cta_h2: The St. Regis Punta Mita earned its place on my list. Let me match you to the right room, time it to the right season, and build the rest of the trip around it.
